_readme: THE BCS RULE PARITY TABLE (slice BCS-S2e) -- ONE case list, consumed by BOTH suites.
WHY IT EXISTS. The browser mirrors the server's two column-confirmation rule chains
(services/boq_bcs/sources.py <-> frontend/src/pages/boq-wizard/bcsColumns.ts). ADR-0010 F1
requires such a mirror to be pinned by a parity test. There was none -- and at BCS-S2b the
server widened to eight amount shapes while the browser silently refused six of them for a
WHOLE SLICE, with every frontend test green. The owner found it by opening a dialog and
seeing an empty list. A green suite on each side separately is exactly what that failure
looked like.
WHY A SHARED CODE, AND NOT A SHARED MESSAGE. The two sides refuse in different voices on
purpose: the server throws a (title, message) pair, the card renders a friendlier sentence.
Pinning the prose would either force one voice on both or pin nothing. So each refusal now
carries a short CODE, minted where the condition is decided, and the CODES are what this
table compares. Conditions and precedence are the contract; wording is not.
WHY PRECEDENCE IS IN HERE AT ALL. Only the success `mode` was ever comparable between the
two sides, so a naive pin would have covered the ten modes and NONE of the refusal chain --
the partial test that makes a gap look closed. The ORDER decides WHICH refusal a bad pick
gets, and a user does not experience a different complaint for the same pick as a wording
nit: it reads as the screen and the server disagreeing about their sheet. Every `beats` case
below is an input that violates TWO rules at once and pins which one answers.
WHERE THIS FILE LIVES, AND WHY. Beside the Python module, because the server is THE
AUTHORITY -- bcsColumns.ts says so in its own docblock and mirrors it. The table describes
the authority's rules; housing it with the client would invert the direction the whole
arrangement depends on. Python reads it with json.load relative to __file__; the vitest suite
takes it as a PLAIN BUNDLER IMPORT of this path, resolved by the toolchain (resolveJsonModule
is on in frontend/tsconfig.json), which is what bcsColumns.test.ts:26 actually does.
CORRECTED AT BCS-S2e-fix. This paragraph used to say the vitest suite read the file with
readFileSync off import.meta.url, 'NOT a bundler import -- no Vite fs-allow question'. Both
halves were false about what SHIPS: that was the ABANDONED first draft (bcsColumns.test.ts's
own docblock records why it was dropped -- the inline decode tripped the ADR-0010 F2 ratchet),
and because the shipped import crosses out of frontend/ the module-resolution question is
raised rather than avoided. It is ANSWERED -- the suite resolves and both sides demonstrably
read this one file -- but a comment claiming a safety property the shipped approach lacks is
worse than no comment, because the next reader plans against it.
ADDING A CASE: add it here once. Both suites pick it up with no edit. Adding a RULE means a
new code in `order`, at its real position, plus a `beats` case against each neighbour it can
actually be constructed against -- and both suites assert `order` against the module's own
declared order, so a code added to one side alone goes red on that side.
THE PRECEDENCE FLOOR IS PER-ADJACENCY, NOT A COUNT (BCS-S2e-fix). Until this slice both
suites asked only for `>= 8` `beats` cases while this table carried 11 -- three cases of
slack, in the one guard whose whole job is to stop a precedence claim going unpinned. The
reviewer proved it: deleting `amount-precedence-kind-beats-shape`, the case labelled below as
THE LOAD-BEARING ONE, left both suites GREEN. That is the same 'looks closed' failure this
table exists to prevent, one level down. Both suites now walk each side's chain PAIRWISE and
require every adjacent pair to be covered by a real `beats` case or declared unconstructible
in `unconstructible_adjacencies` below -- so a NAMED case cannot be dropped in silence, and
no hand-maintained number has to be bumped when a case is added.

codes.unknown_column: A picked letter is not a mapped column on this sheet.
codes.duplicate_column: The same letter appears twice in the pick.
codes.aliased_columns: Two DIFFERENT letters resolve to one (value_field, value_key, rate_subkey), so summing them counts one number twice.
codes.wrong_class: A mapped column of the wrong class for this side (a rate on the amount side, an amount on the quantity side, a description on either).
codes.mixed_kinds: AMOUNT ONLY -- a combined TOTAL picked beside a supply/install HALF it already contains.
codes.mixed_shapes: Scalar column(s) mixed with per-area ones.
codes.too_many_scalars: More than one scalar column of a single kind.

too_many_scalars.why: A column's scalar kind IS its value_field, so two picks of one scalar kind necessarily share a resolved identity and `aliased_columns` fires first and SHADOWS this. RETAINED on both sides rather than deleted -- it is the correctly voiced refusal should the duplicate key ever narrow, and dropping a live refusal is a behaviour change of its own. The shadow itself is pinned by the cases named below, on BOTH sides, so the two layers cannot drift apart in silence.

_unconstructible_adjacencies_note: THE EXEMPTION LIST for the per-adjacency precedence floor, and it is DATA so that the
guard never needs hand-editing. Both suites require every ADJACENT pair in each side's
`order` to be covered by a `beats` case OR named here with a reason -- and NEVER both, since
an entry here claiming a pair cannot be built while a case builds it is a false statement,
not a waiver. Each entry is also checked to BE a real adjacency of its side's chain, so a
reorder that strands one goes red instead of quietly widening the exemption.
Only two shapes are exempt, both for reasons about the RULES rather than about effort: a
pick cannot be simultaneously empty and wrong, and a pick that reaches `too_many_scalars`
has already been answered by `aliased_columns` much earlier in the chain.

unconstructible_adjacencies.why: `no_pick` fires only on an EMPTY selection and `unknown_column` needs a letter to be wrong about, so no single input violates both. Not a coverage gap -- an impossibility.

Two scalar totals necessarily share a resolved identity, so `aliased_columns` -- which sits EARLIER than both -- always answers first. `too_many_scalars` can never be the loser to its own neighbour; the shadow that really governs it is pinned instead by `qty-shadow-two-scalar-totals` and by `unreachable`.
As on the quantity side: empty and wrong are mutually exclusive.
As on the quantity side: `aliased_columns` shadows `too_many_scalars` from far earlier in the chain, and `amount-shadow-two-scalar-supplies` is what pins that.

client_only_codes.unruled_combination: The client's (shape, kinds) table miss. The server's equivalent is a deliberate bare KeyError on `_AMOUNT_MODES` -- 'fail loudly rather than mint a plausible mode'. Both are unreachable by construction (every combination the guards permit is in both tables), and the two sides answer DIFFERENTLY on purpose, so this code is deliberately NOT part of the parity vocabulary. Do not add it to `order`.

_descriptors_note: EXACTLY the shape review_screen._build_column_descriptors emits, which is what
bcs._descriptor_index feeds the server and what the card holds client-side. E aliases B
(Zone A quantity on two letters), L aliases D (the scalar total twice), U aliases G (Zone A
combined amount twice) and V aliases J (the scalar supply amount twice) -- review_screen
imposes NO uniqueness on (role, area) across columns, so every one of those is a shape a
real sheet can have, and each is what makes one refusal constructible.

cases.why: The sheet's one scalar Total Quantity column.
Two areas whose SUM is the row's total.
A one-area sheet is per-area, not scalar -- the mode records the SHAPE, not the count.
Shape 1 of 8. BYTE-UNCHANGED since BCS-S1a -- confirmations stored before the widening read back identically.
Shape 2 of 8. The two scalar halves, SUMMED -- most real sheets have no combined Amount column at all.
Addition commutes, so the FORMULA is the same either way. A mode that flipped on pick order would disclose something untrue of the arithmetic.
Shape 3 of 8. THE REVERSAL (owner 2026-08-02): a lone half is ACCEPTED and the mode discloses the one-sidedness.
Shape 4 of 8.
Shape 5 of 8. BYTE-UNCHANGED since BCS-S1a.
Shape 6 of 8, on a single area.
Shape 6 of 8 summing across BOTH axes at once -- area AND kind. The shape BCS-S1a could not express at all.
Shape 7 of 8. One-sided on the KIND axis while still summing on the AREA axis -- the mode says both at once.
Shape 8 of 8.
A single per-area half is still the per-area one-sided shape.
Nothing picked.
Z is not on this sheet.
One bad letter refuses the WHOLE pick -- never a quiet drop.
The same letter necessarily resolves identically, so this violates the aliased rule too. The degenerate case is voiced in its OWN words.
BCS-S1c: B and E are BOTH Zone A quantity. Summing them double-counts the row -- the exact harm the duplicate rule exists to prevent, walked past by a letter-keyed check.
Existing is not enough -- A is a real mapped column, and it is the Description.
The two confirmations are separate questions; a valid answer to one is not a valid answer to the other.
A rate is neither a quantity nor an amount.
A scalar total summed with its own per-area parts counts every quantity twice.
A column the sheet does not have is reported as UNKNOWN -- the more fundamental fact about it -- rather than as a duplicate.
_resolve_picks runs BEFORE every per-side rule, so the duplicate family shadows the class check.
D+B is a shape mix and A is the wrong class; the CLASS check answers first on both sides.

THE SHADOW. Two scalar totals necessarily share a resolved identity, so `too_many_scalars` is unreachable on BOTH sides. Pinned here so the retained-but-shadowed rule cannot quietly start answering on one side only.
Nothing picked.
Z is not on this sheet.
The degenerate case of the aliased rule, voiced in its own words.
G and U are BOTH Zone A's combined amount.
BCS's denominator is what we CHARGE, not the unit price it was derived from.
Widening the KIND axis did NOT widen the class check.
A rate is still not an amount however the rest of the pick is shaped.

ADDED AT BCS-S2e-fix, closing the one edge the S2e net named but did not compare. W's value_field IS the per-area amount field and its ROLE reads as an amount, but its THIRD HOP is missing -- so the number cannot be resolved at all, and both sides must place it OUTSIDE the amount class rather than accept an unresolvable pick. Until this case the two class guards were never compared on the family the net exists for: the server keys on `subkey in _AREA_AMOUNT_KINDS`, the browser on a truthiness test AND a set membership, and only an input like this can tell whether those two agree.

The other half of the same edge, and NOT redundant with it: a null third hop is caught by the browser's truthiness test alone, while an unknown-but-present one ('net') reaches the set membership. Two different lines of the client guard, one line of the server's -- so a client that dropped its membership check would still pass the null case and fail only this one.
THE ONE PIECE OF THE HALF-REFUSAL THAT SURVIVED BCS-S2b. F already CONTAINS J, so the pair counts the supply half twice.
The per-area twin: Zone A's combined amount already contains Zone A's supply.
The pick is refused WHOLE rather than quietly dropping I.
THE UN-RULED SHAPE -- one kind scalar, the other per-area, with NO total anywhere. Refused rather than guessed at; a sheet like this is a ruling, not a bug.
One KIND (total) across two SHAPES, so mixed_kinds cannot fire and the shape rule is the honest answer.
Unknown-first, as on the quantity side.
_resolve_picks precedes the class check.
The CLASS check runs before the kind comparison, because a pick is only placed on the two axes once it is known to be an amount at all.

★ THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. F (scalar total) beside I (per-area supply) violates BOTH axes. The server answers 'the combined Amount already includes the halves', so the card must too -- the same rules in a different order give a different complaint for one input, which a user reads as the screen and the server disagreeing about their sheet.

THE SHADOW on the amount side. NOTE what this is NOT: the pre-S2b 'a sheet has exactly one Amount column' rule, which BCS-S2b made simply FALSE -- a scalar sheet legitimately contributes TWO columns now, its supply and its install.
